action: Lynn comes back to the laundry. The camera takes her from behind for the whole approach and never comes round, so for these fourteen seconds the shot is not about her face - it is about the shopfront she is walking toward: stripped back, brightly lit, a ladder, paint tins, plastic sheeting, a scooter parked out front. Last time she stood at this address she was the one asking, and he said no before he named a price. Now the place is being rebuilt. That is the editorial point and it is the whole reason the shot runs this long in a film whose median shot is three seconds: the money is put on screen before anybody speaks a word about it, and the shot withholds both faces while it does. A writer can use this as the arrival and as the state of the place; the meeting itself is not in it.
